messages:
taylor: quick thought: build a tiny 'web onramp' proxy shim at the edge that accepts simple JSON from the browser SDK and translates into our internal protobuf/gRPC calls. makes frontends trivial, avoids grpc-web dependency. main tradeoffs: extra translation hop, telemetry/quotas mapping, and auth/CORS edge cases. anyone object? :thinking_face:
jess: ergonomics are compelling. main operational worries: Console dashboards might lose per-model or per-route breakdown if translation collapses routes. and CORS + cookie flows are fiddly.
omar: quota/billing concern: the shim must map client creds to tenant ids before any aggregation. otherwise we misattribute usage. gateway should inject an authoritative X-RW-TENANT header into translated requests.
sam: alternative is forcing grpc-web on clients so we keep streaming and exact accounting. that's ideal but heavier for product teams. If we ship the shim, ensure header passthrough and emit a translation trace/span.
taylor: proposal sketch: shim accepts POST JSON, validates creds, resolves tenant, then emits translated gRPC with headers: X-RW-ORIG-ROUTE, X-RW-MODEL, X-RW-CLIENT-TYPE, X-RW-TENANT. also emit events translate.start and translate.end.
omar: quota counting decision: count optimistic/approximate units at the edge for low-latency enforcement, then reconcile asynchronously with accurate runtime counts. reconciliation job should emit metrics reconcile.delta and reconcile.rate and alert if tenant delta_rate > 0.5%.
jess: rollout plan: feature-flag the shim; canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h windows. guardrails: translate.p95 < 20ms, translate.error < 0.2%, quota_mismatch_rate < 0.3%. require translation span in traces so Console shows edge vs runtime timing.
deploy-bot: CI note: add canary pipeline in eng-platform, track metrics translate.success, translate.latency_p95, model.latency_p95, quota_mismatch_rate. auto-pause on SLO breach.
taylor: cool, i'll draft a short RFC with header mapping, telemetry events, reconcile job outline, and the canary steps. will @jess and @omar for review. thanks everyone :sparkles:
